```{r}

# Step 1: Load Data 

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tableone)
library(gtsummary)

setwd("~/Downloads")
patients <- read.csv("patients.csv")
head(patients, 4)

```


```{r}

# Step2: Set Data 

data <-patients |> 
  mutate(
    drug_count =drugA+drugB+drugC, 
    
    treatment_type = case_when (
      drug_count >1 ~ "Combo Therapy", 
      drug_count == 0 ~ "No Therapy",
      drugA ==1  ~ "Drug A",
      drugB ==1  ~ "Drug B", 
      drugC ==1  ~ "Drug C"
    ),
    
    birth_dt = as.Date(birth_dt),
    diagnosis_dt = as.Date(diagnosis_dt),
    
    Age = as.numeric(floor(interval(birth_dt, diagnosis_dt)/years(1))), 
    
    Gender = factor(gender, levels = c("M", "F"), labels =c("Male", "Female"))
  )

head(data,4)
str(data)

```

```{r, echo=TRUE}

# Step3: Create a Table 

library(gtsummary)


table<-data |> 
  mutate(treatment_type =factor(treatment_type, 
                                levels =c ("Drug A", "DrugB", "Drug C", "Combo Therapy", "No Therapy")))|>
  tbl_summary(
    by = treatment_type, 
    include = c(Gender, Age),
    label = list(Age~"Age at Diagnosis"),
    type = list(Age ~ "continuous2"),  ## add two rows? 
    statistic = list(Age ~ c("{median} ({p25}, {p75})", "{mean} ({sd})"))
  ) |> 
  bold_labels()|>
  # This removes the N = XXX from all treatment columns
  modify_header (
    all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**", # Removes total counts (N=X) and strips out the superscript numbers
    label~ "**Total Patients**"
    )|>
  modify_footnote(everything()~NA) 

table
```
```{r, echo =TRUE}

#Step 4: Logistic Regression

Logi<-glm(overall_response ~ Age + treatment_type, data = data, family =binomial)
summary(Logi)

Logi_summary <-coef(summary(Logi))
Logi_ci <-confint(Logi)


age_response <- data.frame(
  Var             = rownames(Logi_summary),
  coefficient     = Logi_summary[, "Estimate"],
  standard_errors = Logi_summary[, "Std. Error"],
  odd_ratios      = exp(Logi_summary[, "Estimate"]),
  odd_ci_lower    = exp(Logi_ci[, 1]), # Column 1 is 2.5% (Lower)
  odd_ci_upper    = exp(Logi_ci[, 2]), # Column 2 is 97.5% (Upper)
  p_value         = Logi_summary[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
)

print(age_response)

```
```{r, echo =TRUE}

# Step 5: Kaplan-Meier Plot with a Risk Table -- need data cleaning 
library(survival)
library(survminer)

## Clean Data: Censor = 0, Event (Death =1)

# 1. Time, Event Vars

data <-data |> 
  mutate(event = ifelse(is.na(death_dt), 0, 1),
         
         death_dt = as.Date(death_dt),
         last_visit_dt = as.Date(last_visit_dt),
         
         time = ifelse(event ==0,as.numeric(last_visit_dt-diagnosis_dt), as.numeric(death_dt-diagnosis_dt)),
         time_months = time/30.4375,
         time_years = time/365.25
         )
        

# 2. Fit the Kaplan-Meier survival curve for Overall Survival by treatment_type 

km_fit <- survfit(Surv(time_years,event) ~ treatment_type, data=data)


# 3. Plot the curve with the risk table
ggsurvplot(
  km_fit, 
  data =data,
  risk.table =TRUE, 
  pval = TRUE, 
  conf.int =FALSE, 
  xlab = "Time in years",
  break.time.by=12, 
  palette = c("#E7B800", "#2E9FDF", "#FC4E07", "#00AFBB", "#868686")
)

```
```{r, echo =TRUE}


# Step 6: Median Overall Survival Time + 95% CI

km_fit # to see median and 95%CI 

km_fit_loglog <-survfit (
  Surv(time_years, event) ~ treatment_type, data=data, 
  conf.type = "log-log"
)

km_fit_loglog_summary <- summary(km_fit_loglog)$table
km_fit_loglog_summary


table1 <-data.frame(
  #Var = rownames(km_fit_loglog_summary),
  Median = km_fit_loglog_summary[, "median"],
  CL_lower=km_fit_loglog_summary[, "0.95LCL"],
  CL_upper=km_fit_loglog_summary[,"0.95UCL"]
)


print(table1)

```
